direction: Restrained low-poly forms, subdued colors, deadpan expressions and worn retro vehicles.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: second-round alien character exploration for Mayhem Meadows, a low-poly third-person cartoon driving game with chaotic small-town humor.
Primary request: make aliens that are goofy through attitude and body language, with dry absurdist humor rather than childish cuteness. Include a recognizable classic grey alien. The previous round had huge shiny friendly eyes, very large heads, tiny bodies, big trainers, candy colors and a preschool mascot feeling; move decisively toward scruffy, deadpan retro sci-fi characters for a comedic game.
Scene/backdrop: pale warm-gray concept-sheet background, three well-separated characters in one wide horizontal lineup, subtle ground shadows.
Style/medium: simple faceted low-poly 3D game model concepts, matte flat colors, visible polygon planes, angular primitive limbs and hands, simple dark facial marks. Modest geometry suitable for a procedural Three.js game. Stylized and cartoonish, with restrained proportions and slightly awkward anatomy. Not photorealistic and not cinematic animated-movie polish.
Subject A: a classic grey alien, recognizably slender ash-gray hairless humanoid, moderately enlarged bald oval head tapering to a small chin, traditional slanted almond-shaped black eyes with no oversized white eyeballs or sparkling highlights, tiny nostrils, thin horizontal mouth, long arms and fingers, narrow shoulders, simple long limbs and bare flat feet. Neutral slouch, one hip cocked, one skeptical brow ridge, holding a small clipboard down by its thigh as if inspecting a parking violation. Expression mildly unimpressed and subtly comic, never sinister. No clothing on its simple smooth featureless stylized body.
Subject B: an olive-gray alien with a long blunt face, two small narrow dark eyes beneath heavy angular brows, low protruding ears, average human-like head-to-body ratio around 1:5, slightly hunched torso, boxy rust-colored mechanic coveralls, rolled sleeves and scuffed modest work boots; one hand resting on the hip, resigned expression.
Subject C: a tall muted blue-gray alien with a broad low brow and flat elongated head, small asymmetrical dark eyes, narrow smirking mouth, long nose-like center ridge, a faded mustard short jacket over simple charcoal trousers, long lanky limbs and sensible narrow shoes; looking sideways with a caught-in-the-act posture, hands tucked behind the back.
Composition/framing: full-body elevated three-quarter-front character views, each clearly separated, consistent scale, large legible silhouettes. Small panel letters A, B, C only, no other text.
Lighting/mood: plain daylight-like illumination, gentle simple shadows. Goofy through slouching, impatience, incompetence and deadpan expressions. Small-town nuisance energy.
Color palette: ash gray, olive gray, dusty blue-gray, faded mustard, rust, charcoal; subdued colors compatible with a pastel coastal game.
Constraints: original designs; classic grey archetype clearly recognizable; bodies simplified like low-poly town residents; modelable with primitive meshes; no plush texture, no giant sneakers, no overalls on toddlers, no huge round shiny eyes, no big toothy smiles, no chibi proportions, no cute mascot look. No menacing grin, claws, gore, anatomical detail, exposed anatomy, horror lighting, weapons, logos or watermark.

concepts.A: Classic worn gray disc with narrow cockpit glazing
concepts.B: Secondhand olive-and-rust utility saucer with a roof rack

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: second-round UFO flying saucer exploration for Mayhem Meadows, a low-poly third-person cartoon driving game with dry small-town comedy.
Primary request: two more mature goofy flying saucer concepts: classic retro sci-fi discs treated like slightly battered practical vehicles. The humor comes from wonky engineering and mundane vehicle details, not toy styling or childish cute faces. Match the simple faceted primitive-based geometry of the game's chunky cars and pastel coastal buildings.
Scene/backdrop: pale warm-gray studio concept-sheet backdrop, two large craft side by side, generous clear space and soft ground shadows. No environment or characters.
Style/medium: restrained low-poly 3D game asset renders, visible flat-shaded facets, matte painted metal represented with simple flat color patches, very sparse broad wear marks, simple dark cockpit glazing, minimal geometry. Neither photorealism nor smooth glossy toy renders.
Subject A: a classic grey-alien flying saucer, wide shallow dull aluminum-gray disc with a simple raised central dome, a very thin dark wraparound cockpit slit beneath the dome, understated charcoal underside, three short spindly landing struts with broad flat pads. A few broad planar panel seams, one slightly crooked aerial and one mismatched replacement panel. Unmistakable classic 1950s flying saucer silhouette, understated and comically utilitarian, no weapon ports.
Subject B: an olive-gray and faded rust-orange municipal-looking saucer, low broad circular hull, squat angular cockpit integrated into the center, simple flat dark windshield panes, thick slightly dented peripheral bumper, a couple of rectangular service hatches, one small amber warning lamp on a stubby stalk, three chunky short retractable feet. A lopsided roof-mounted flat luggage rack with a spare circular panel strapped down. Feels like a secondhand flying delivery vehicle with absurd engineering.
Composition/framing: full craft in consistent three-quarter views slightly above eye level, enough underside visible to read landing gear. One small clean side-profile study beneath each main design. Clearly different silhouettes, restrained detailing. Small panel letters A and B only, no other text.
Lighting/mood: plain daylight-like studio light, subtle ambient shading, relaxed dry comic personality rather than menace.
Color palette: muted gray aluminum, charcoal, olive-gray, faded rust and small dull amber highlights.
Constraints: keep the circular flying-saucer silhouettes; use primitive meshes and broad readable shapes suitable for a simple browser game. No faces or characters, no candy colors, no oversized glowing round bumper lights, no glossy toy look, no dense machinery, no chrome photorealism, no threatening weapons or spikes, no smoke, no dramatic sci-fi scene, no text, logos or watermark.
